stories.article_text_excerpt: BRUSSELS — The European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas on Sunday was forced to cancel the launch of a new high-level group made up of former political and military leaders following pressure from EU member countries, in what could prove another blow to the former Estonian prime minister. Kallas is leading a fierce behind-the-scenes push against Franco-German plans to overhaul the European External Action Service, the bloc’s diplomatic corps. Those plans on paper aim to reinforce Kallas’ formal role, but her allies fear they could allow the European Commission to take greater control of foreign policy. The high-level group — which Kallas described as bringing together “the brightest minds” to come up with ideas to fulfill EU defense gaps “in the shortest timeframe possible in the most effective way” — was seen by some diplomats as part of this resistance. “It’s her way to remain relevant,” said a senior EU diplomat, who like others quoted in this story was granted anonymity to speak freely. Advertisement Advertisement Kallas has been in intense competition with the Commission over these plans, but an EU official said the reason for the cancellation was pressure from some capitals.

During Poland’s 2025 presidential campaign, politicians began portraying Ukrainians in Poland as freeloaders straining the country’s public finances. The group murdered tens of thousands of Poles during an ethnic-cleansing campaign in 1943-1945, although it also fought against the Soviet Union. stories.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

stories.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
stories.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

stories.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
stories.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

stories.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare

"The police operation has ended," said an airport spokeswoman. Federal police, responsible for transportation security in Germany , had evacuated BER Terminal 1 at around 5:45 p.m. after a woman reportedly told security staff at a service point that she had a dangerous substance in her luggage. "A potential threat from the unidentified substance could not be ruled out," the police spokesperson told the dpa news agency. Police then gave the all-clear at around 8:45 p.m. and confirmed that nobody had been in danger at any point. Police initially provided no information as to the nature of the substance in question, with analysis results expected in the coming days. stories.summary: Haze is a recurring seasonal problem in Southeast Asia, where smoke from forest and peat fires in Indonesia can travel across national borders and affect neighbouring Malaysia, Brunei and Singapore.

stories.summary: With less than two days to go Kazakhstan stands a good chance to become the overall winner of the 6th Nomad Games held in Kyrgyzstan. With 55 medals won the largest country of Central Asia is well ahead of the other teams.

stories.summary: The mistrial now puts the murder case - and Clancy's future - in limbo as to whether she will be held criminally liable in the deaths of her three kids.
